newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dowa Mining lifts copper refinery capacity.
newsitem.headline: Dowa Mining lifts copper refinery capacity.

text.p: Dowa Mining Co is raising the electrolytic copper refining capacity of its Kosaka complex to 5,000 tonnes per month from about 4,400 tonnes and will operate at full capacity from October, a spokeswoman said on Friday.
The company is also considering a further lift in refining capacity to 6,000 tonnes per month, she said, confirming a report this morning in the daily Nikkei Sangyo Shimbun.
The move will bring electrolytic refining capacity closer to Kosaka's smelting capacity of 6,000 tonnes of copper blister per month.
Excess blister is sent to the Onahama smelter, which is jointly owned by Dowa and five other Japanese copper companies, for refining.
The spokeswoman added that Dowa is still considering a 20,000 tonne-per-year boost in zinc refining capacity at the Iijima smelter, in which it owns a majority share.
Iijima, Japan's largest zinc refinery, has an annual capacity of 156,000 tonnes.
